input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?

Yes, I can try to follow your instructions, but I do get a bit nervous with technical things. Right now, at the top of my phone, I see that the signal is excellent, it says 5G, and there’s a little icon that looks like data is on. The battery is at 80%. I don’t see anything about Airplane Mode. What should I do next?

I haven’t really tried using the internet on my phone, since I mostly just use it for calls, texts, and taking photos. Regular text messages seem to go through just fine—it’s only the picture messages that aren’t working. What should I do to check the MMS settings?

I checked, and it looks like there isn’t an MMSC URL set in my phone’s APN settings. I’m not really sure what that means, but is that something that could be causing the problem? What should I do next?

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to restart my phone now—will that erase any of my photos or messages? I get a bit worried about losing things when I reboot. Could you reassure me before I do this?

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—this is more complicated than I expected.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is turned off on my phone. Also, my messaging app already has permission for SMS, storage, and phone. Is there anything else that could be causing the problem?
If you think a human agent could help, then yes, please transfer me. I just want to be able to send pictures to my family again. Thank you for trying to help me—I hope they can figure it out!

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture messaging) issue. First, I’ll need to identify your account to check for any service or data issues that might be affecting MMS. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you through the steps to resolve your MMS problem.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?

Thank you for providing your information. To help you with your MMS issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks on your phone. This will help us identify what’s causing the problem.

Are you able to perform some simple checks and actions on your phone if I give you step-by-step instructions? If so, please let me know, and we’ll start by checking your phone’s status bar for any obvious issues like Airplane Mode or signal problems.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Yes, I can try to follow your instructions, but I do get a bit nervous with technical things. Right now, at the top of my phone, I see that the signal is excellent, it says 5G, and there’s a little icon that looks like data is on. The battery is at 80%. I don’t see anything about Airplane Mode. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking those details. Since you have excellent signal, 5G connectivity, and data is on, that’s a good start. The next step is to check if your mobile data is working for other apps (like browsing the web) and to confirm that your phone’s MMS settings are correct.

Could you please let me know:
1. Are you able to use the internet on your phone (for example, can you browse websites or use apps that require data)?
2. Have you noticed any issues with regular text messages (SMS), or is it only picture messages (MMS) that aren’t working?

Once you confirm this, I’ll guide you through checking your MMS settings and permissions.

I haven’t really tried using the internet on my phone, since I mostly just use it for calls, texts, and taking photos. Regular text messages seem to go through just fine—it’s only the picture messages that aren’t working. What should I do to check the MMS settings?

Thank you for clarifying. Since regular texts are working and you have good signal and data, the issue may be with your MMS settings or permissions.

Let’s start by checking your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are important for MMS to work. Could you please check your phone’s APN settings and let me know if you see an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed? If you’re not sure how to check this, I can guide you through the steps.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to check your APN/MMSC settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked, and it looks like there isn’t an MMSC URL set in my phone’s APN settings. I’m not really sure what that means, but is that something that could be causing the problem? What should I do next?

Yes, not having an MMSC URL set in your APN settings can definitely cause MMS (picture messages) to stop working. The MMSC URL is required for your phone to send and receive MMS.

The next step is to reset your APN settings to the default values. This will usually restore the correct MMSC URL and other necessary settings. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and then reboot your device?

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to restart my phone now—will that erase any of my photos or messages? I get a bit worried about losing things when I reboot. Could you reassure me before I do this?

Rest assured, restarting (rebooting) your phone will not erase any of your photos, messages, or personal data. A reboot simply turns your phone off and back on, refreshing its system and applying any new settings—like the APN changes you just made.

It’s a safe and common step in troubleshooting, and all your files and apps will remain intact.

When you’re ready, please go ahead and restart your phone. After it powers back on, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works. If you still have trouble, I’ll guide you through the next steps.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—this is more complicated than I expected.

Thank you for your patience. I understand this can be frustrating, but we’ll keep working through it together. Since resetting the APN and rebooting didn’t solve the issue, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling turned on can interfere with sending MMS.
2. Does your messaging app have permission to access storage and SMS? The app needs these permissions to send and receive picture messages.

Would you like step-by-step instructions to check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled and how to check your messaging app’s permissions?
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, storage, phone.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is turned off on my phone. Also, my messaging app already has permission for SMS, storage, and phone. Is there anything else that could be causing the problem?
